# Paperlab

> Physical, realistic paper as a React component. A sheet is a real 3D mesh — content is a texture on geometry that genuinely bends, so text and images curl with perfect continuity. Preset-driven, serializable, agent-first.

Install: `npm i paperlab three @react-three/fiber gsap` (React ≥ 19, three ≥ 0.160)

## Core API

- `<Paper />` — one sheet, owns its own <Canvas>, fills its parent (parent needs a height!). Props: preset (name or object), sheet {width,height,thickness}, stock ('printer'|'thermal'|'kraft'|'newsprint'|'vellum'|'photo-gloss'|'sticker'), content ({type:'image',src,alt} — src may be empty, meaning bare stock | {type:'text',text,size,weight,align,valign,tracking,lineHeight,padding} | {type:'card',title,body,note,rule,ruled,align} — the paper-artifact type: index card, library due-date card, museum label, telegram slip, quote sheet | {type:'receipt',store,items,...}), behavior, surface {grain,deckle,creaseLines,aging,perforation}, physics, interactive, autoplay, reducedMotion.
- `<PaperMesh />` — the same, canvas-less, for existing React Three Fiber scenes.
- `<PaperField />` — many sheets, one instanced draw call. Props: images | papers, preset, layout ('ring'|'fan'|'spread'|'pile'|'wall'|'spill'|'sweep'|'book'|'accordion'|'rack'|'colonnade'|'sheet'), layoutOptions, motion {driver:'autoplay'|'drag'|'none', speed}, entrance {type:'rise'|'scatter'|'none', stagger}. Layouts receive the field's sheet size, so contact layouts (book/accordion/rack/wall/sweep) arrange by real edges. Layouts pose sheets AND set a per-sheet `bias` (0 = flat, 1 = as configured) so one draw call can bend each sheet differently. `<PaperField>` fits its own camera to the layout's poses — don't hand-place one. A preset's raw `deformers` stack overrides its `behavior` in fields exactly as it does for `<Paper>`. A `sheet` layout renders a stamp block on a shared backing; slots with `states` make the field interactive (per-paper hover/press/pick). `<DropZone id bounds={{position,size}} accept={['glob-*']} onPlace={(paper, zone) => …} />` children are drop targets for picked papers.
- `<PaperStage />` — **imported from `paperlab/stage`, not `paperlab`** (it is the only part of the library that needs the `@react-three/postprocessing` + `postprocessing` optional peers, and a subpath is what keeps them optional). Paper as architecture: banners arranged along a walk, with a figure walking it. Owns its Canvas (`<PaperStageScene />` is the canvas-less twin). Props: text (string split across banners a line at a time, or string[] used as given), count, preset (shared paper behind every banner — defaults to a tall vellum banner), papers | images (per-banner slots, as in field mode), layout (default 'colonnade' — the one built to arrange along a walk), layoutOptions, stage (see below), progress (0..1 along the walk; **bind it to scroll and the page scrolls the walk** — omit it and the figure walks on its own clock), quality ('auto'|'low'|'medium'|'high', default 'auto' — adapts to the machine), onQualityChange, reducedMotion. The one invariant: the layout, the figure, the camera and the light source all read the SAME walk, so they cannot disagree.
- `stage={{ path, shot, figure, lighting, showFigure, source, ground, room, grade }}` — validated by the exported `stageSchema`. path: a walk, usually `walks[name]` where name is 'straight'|'bend'|'ess'|'ring'|'spiral' (`getWalk(name)`), or `createWalkPath({points, closed})` for your own. shot: {shot: 'follow'|'lead'|'low'|'wide', …}. figure: {height, speed, stride, swing, color, gait:'auto'|'walk'|'run', model}. `gait` defaults to 'auto', which breaks into a run at the Froude number (~2.1 units/s for a 1.75m figure, and sooner for a shorter one). `model` is a URL for a rigged glTF/GLB to replace the capsule silhouette — the asset is the app's to host, never the library's; its clip is scrubbed by DISTANCE so the feet cannot skate, it is scaled to `height` off its own bounds, drawn as a silhouette because the nave is backlit, and anything that fails to load falls back to the capsules. lighting defaults to 'nave' (stage mode is built for it; the others are front-lit). source is the bright void the walk resolves toward plus its cyclorama; ground is the floor that catches the shadows — `ground.slab` sets the width of one poured slab, and the seams are the scale cue. room is {enabled, height, color}: a ceiling, so the haze has a far surface to settle on and the source has somewhere to spill. **`showFigure` now defaults to FALSE** — the room carries scale, and the stage is navigable, so the person in the hall is the viewer. grade is the print — {bloom, threshold (LINEAR light, default 1.6, above 1 on purpose), vignette, grain} — and needs the OPTIONAL peers `@react-three/postprocessing` + `postprocessing`; `<Paper>` never pulls them in, and it only runs on the `high` quality tier (measured: it costs ~40ms a frame on a software rasterizer). Stage presets: `stagePresets`, `getStagePreset(id)`, `listStagePresets()` — 'nave', 'procession', 'cloister', 'threshold', 'archive', 'ribbon'. Export helpers mirror the paper ones: `buildStageAgentPayload`, `buildStageComponentSource`, `describeStage`, `diffStage`.
- Ref API: play(), pause(), set('progress', v), getProgress(), snapshot(), toJSON(), state, sendState(event).

## Behaviors (behavior={{ type, ...params }})

peel {progress, corner ('auto' resolves outward in a sheet field), radius} · unroll {progress, tightness, sway} · flip {progress, spine, radius} · letter-fold {progress, crease} · hang {wind, sag} · fly {flutter, curve} · fall {flutter, curl} · carry {grab, stiffness, flutter, lag, drive} (a held paper drooping from its pinch point) · flight {wind:[x,y,z], gustiness, tumble, path:'drift'|'loop', respawn, range} (free paper travelling across the scene) · crumple {progress, coarseness, ball, seed} (a sheet crushed in a fist — an irregular crease network; the densest geometry of any deformer) · ribbon {pool, curl, drape} (a strip hung the full drop of a room, pooling where it lands) · settle {relax, lift, corner, slack} (a sheet that has landed and relaxed — the pose after `fall`, and static: it is over)

## Physics

Idle (compose with behaviors): 'float' 'tumble' 'dangle' 'taped' 'breeze'. Cloth (exclusive with behavior — schema-enforced): physics={{type:'cloth', pins:'top-edge'|'top-corners'|'corner'|'none', wind, stiffness, gravity}}. Interactive cloth is grabbable.

## Presets

Built-ins: receipt-unroll, letter-fold, vintage-note, hero-peel, page-flip, hanging-poster, pinned-sheet, flying-note, blank-sheet, photo-print, typed-note, postage-stamp, crumpled-note, settled-sheet, paper-ribbon. Presets are .paper JSON validated by the exported zod paperConfigSchema; helpers: getPreset, parsePreset, serializePreset, diffConfig, buildAgentPayload, describeConfig.
- A `.paper` file someone shares IS a preset object: `import p from './x.paper.json'` then `<Paper preset={p} />`, or `registerPreset('x', p)` to name it. `preset` accepts a string OR a config object — never expand a shared .paper into individual props.

## Interaction states (M6)

A preset may carry `states`: overrides-on-base diffs keyed rest/hover/pressed/picked/placed (`{states: {initial:'rest', states: {hover: {overrides: {behavior:{progress:0.4}}, transition: {duration:0.25, ease:'power2.out'}}}, pickThreshold: 0.08}}`). Triggers are built in: hover/press on pointer, drag past pickThreshold tears a stamp off its sheet (perforation edges facing neighbors flip to 'torn' automatically), release over a DropZone settles it (snap → press → flatten, then onPlace fires), release elsewhere flutters it back — torn stays torn. Field slots take a `states` override layer of their own. Keyboard flow ships automatically: focus a paper, Enter picks, arrows move between zones, Enter places, Esc returns.

## Pitfalls

1. Blank canvas = parent has no height (the classic R3F bug — <Paper> fills its parent).
2. cloth + behavior together throws by design: cloth owns the vertices.
3. prefers-reduced-motion freezes behaviors at their pose and disables physics/entrances automatically.
4. No WebGL → automatic flat DOM fallback; a hidden DOM mirror of the content always renders (use it for E2E assertions).

## Verify after integrating

Run the dev server; the exported describeConfig(config) returns the one-line visual you should see (e.g. 'a store receipt for "acme.dev" on thermal paper stock (1×2.6), unrolling from a paper roll at the bottom, torn (deckled) bottom edge').
